explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Wisdom does the opposite of whispering in a back room. She "…calls out in the street…" and "…lifts her voice in the square…" and she makes her speech "…at the city gates…" (Proverbs 1:20-21). Those are out in the open, not in a quiet room.

That's right, friend. Wisdom doesn't hide in a quiet room. She "…calls out in the street…" "…lifts her voice in the square…" and "cries aloud" in the main concourse (Proverbs 1:20-21). Her speech happens at the city gates, right where the people are. It's open to anyone passing through.

Yes, ma'am, yes, sir, that's it! Wisdom asks, "How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?" (Proverbs 1:22). So the simple ones get company. The scoffers love their scorn, and the fools hate knowledge. That's a whole crowd Wisdom is calling out.

Good guess, but the text doesn't name priests or kings here. Wisdom turns to "scoffers" and "fools" right after the simple ones (Proverbs 1:22). The scoffers delight in their scorn, and the fools hate knowledge. Those are the ones she names.

That's a caring guess, friend, but it's not who she names. After the simple ones, Wisdom speaks to "scoffers" and "fools" (Proverbs 1:22). Scoffers delight in their scorn, and fools hate knowledge. Widows and orphans aren't in this speech.

explanations.answer: they've ignored her for a long time
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, friend! Wisdom asks, "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22). Then she says they "…refused my call…" and "…neglected all my counsel…" (Proverbs 1:24-25). I think that's why she asks. Her question comes after they've turned her down.

explanations.answer: she just arrived in their city
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text never says she just arrived. It says she "…calls out in the street…" (Proverbs 1:20). Her question, "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22), is about what the simple ones are doing. Then she says they "…refused my call…" (Proverbs 1:24).

explanations.answer: she wants to know the time
explanations.explanation: Ha! I wish she were just checking her watch, baker. But "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22) isn't about a clock. It's aimed at the simple ones and their simple ways. Then she says they "…refused my call…" (Proverbs 1:24).

explanations.answer: made her words known to them
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend! Wisdom says, "If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you." (Proverbs 1:23). Those are two gifts that were ready to go. All it took was repenting at her rebuke.

Silver sounds nice, friend, but it's not on her list. Wisdom says she would have "…poured out my spirit on you…" and "…made my words known to you." (Proverbs 1:23). The offer was her spirit and her words. Nothing about silver is in the verse.

explanations.answer: made them rulers of the city
explanations.explanation: Mayor Papa Dorin has a nice ring, but no. Wisdom says she would have "…poured out my spirit on you…" and "…made my words known to you." (Proverbs 1:23). That's what she held out. She doesn't mention ruling the city.

Not this time, friend. Wisdom says the opposite. They "…neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction…" (Proverbs 1:25). So it wasn't half and half. They turned down the counsel and the correction both.

Yes, friend, that's false! Wisdom says they "…neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction…" (Proverbs 1:25). They didn't take the counsel and skip the correction. They passed on both, and that's the whole point of her complaint.

Yes, friend, that's what she says! "Then they will call on me, but I will not answer…" (Proverbs 1:28). The very people who ignored her will be calling her name when trouble hits. Tough to hear, I know. This is the part where I want to say it gently.

That's a fair picture of a scary moment, but it's not in her words. Wisdom says, "Then they will call on me, but I will not answer…" (Proverbs 1:28). Their move is to call on her. Running to the hills isn't mentioned.

People do love a good blame game, friend. But Wisdom doesn't say that here. She says, "Then they will call on me, but I will not answer…" (Proverbs 1:28). So they call on her, and nobody gets blamed in the verse.

Ooh, this one stings, friend. Wisdom says the opposite: "they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me." (Proverbs 1:28). They seek her hard, and they still don't find her. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the speech.

Right, and it's a heavy one. Wisdom says, "they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me." (Proverbs 1:28). They look hard for her, and she's not found. So the answer is False. I think that's a verse to sit with for a second.

That's it, friend! Wisdom says, "For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD." (Proverbs 1:29). Hating knowledge is one half, and choosing not to fear the LORD is the other. She puts them side by side in the same verse.

Close, but this one is true, friend. Wisdom says, "For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD." (Proverbs 1:29). Both things are in the same verse. Hating knowledge and not fearing the LORD go together in her words.

explanations.answer: they get what their own choices bring
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! Wisdom says, "So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices." (Proverbs 1:31). Fruit is what grows from what you planted. So their own way brings its own result. It's like throwing out the recipe and then being surprised by the cookies.

explanations.answer: they finally have plenty to eat
explanations.explanation: I see where you're going, friend, but this fruit isn't a snack. Wisdom says "…they will eat the fruit of their own way…" (Proverbs 1:31). It's a picture of what their own way produces. Right after, she says they'll be "…filled with their own devices."

explanations.answer: someone else pays for their choices
explanations.explanation: Not here, friend. Wisdom says "…they will eat the fruit of their own way…" (Proverbs 1:31). They're the ones eating it. The result of their own way lands on them, and it's followed by being "…filled with their own devices."

That's right, friend, and what a way to end! Wisdom finishes with, "But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil." (Proverbs 1:33). After all those hard words, she ends on a promise. Whoever listens gets safety. I love that she lands there.

Good news, friend. This one is true! Her last words are, "But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil." (Proverbs 1:33). The speech was heavy, but it ends with a promise for whoever listens.
